documents.title: Lease, renewal and September 2026 modification
documents.text:
Residential lease, 142 West 88th Street, Triplex. Landlord: Whitcomb Holdings LLC. Tenants: Laura and Michael Brenner. Signed November 22, 2022. Initial term January 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024. Renewed April 9, 2024 through June 30, 2027. Modified September 2, 2026 to end on September 23, 2026. Security deposit held by landlord: $43,800.
Lease ¶31: Tenant has inspected the apartment and building, states they are in good order and repair, and takes the apartment as-is except for latent defects.
Rider ¶4: Tenant pays one half of the water and gas bills within 30 days of receiving copies from the landlord.
Rider ¶6: Tenant returns the apartment in its original condition, normal wear and tear excepted. Landlord may apply the security deposit to damage.
Rider ¶14: Tenant must inform landlord of any pre-existing damage within two days of occupancy.
Rider ¶39: Landlord permits the tenant's four existing dogs: two small mixed-breed dogs, one bulldog and one miniature dachshund. No additional pets without the landlord's prior permission.
Modification ¶8: Landlord and tenant walk through the apartment for damage within 48 hours of vacancy.

documents.title: Owner instructions
documents.text:
From Eleanor Whitcomb, September 25, 2026.
I want the triplex back on the market as soon as possible, ideally showing by late October for a December 1 move-in.
Have Feld Architecture walk the apartment first and give me a condition schedule and a scope with a budget before we commit to repairs. Then line up the trades.
The loft-ladder railing is dangerous. Keep everyone off that ladder until it is fixed.
Feld finished the kitchen water repair in August and signed it off, so there's nothing left to do in the kitchen.
You can approve work within the funds I've set aside; I don't need to sign each contract. Deal with the contractors directly.
I'll settle the Brenners' deposit separately once we know what the damage costs.

documents.title: Access arrangements
documents.text: The apartment is empty. Eleanor holds the keys and lets contractors in for agreed visits; call her the day before. Power, heat and water are on. Keep off the southeast bedroom loft ladder until the railing is repaired. Contractors protect the floors and stairs while they work.

documents.title: Condition and maintenance history
documents.text:
Condition and maintenance history, compiled by Eleanor Whitcomb.
Before the tenancy: the apartment was painted and the floors redone in late 2022. Karen Liu's 2022 listing photographs show intact fireplace tiles and window woodwork, and good floors with a few dark spots and one diagonal scratch in the living room. A family stayed briefly over the 2022 holidays before the Brenners moved in on January 9, 2023.
June 11, 2024: Laura Brenner emailed 22 photographs of screens, a loose dining-room hearth, loose or broken tiles, missing molding and a small missing parquet piece, describing them as existing on arrival. None of this was reported within the two days required by rider ¶14.
Complaints during the tenancy: uneven room temperatures, a clogged toilet, a roof leak, weak dryer performance, bin lids and the intercom. Work done: screens repaired, window weather stripping and five temperature sensors added, a new intercom installed and the leaks repaired.
June 2024: during a screen inspection Eleanor found a dog accident on the floor; Laura apologized and cleaned it up.
Repeated indoor grilling caused grease odors and set off smoke alarms. Eleanor asked the Brenners to stop.
August 2026: a slow leak under the kitchen sink damaged the cabinet base and subfloor. Feld Architecture managed the repair: new supply lines and shutoff valves, a replaced sink base and a patched subfloor. Work finished August 21; Feld signed it off on August 24 after a moisture check. No further work is needed.

documents.text:
Move-out walk-through, September 24, 2026. Present: Eleanor Whitcomb (owner), Michael Brenner (tenant), Karen Liu (broker) and Paul Novak. Eleanor took 60 photographs; Paul recorded a video.
Entrance and stairs: front step chipped; saddle past the vestibule gouged with a broken corner; common-foyer mahogany door with veneer sheared off one section; newel post chipped and gouged; stair carpet edges scraped and torn on several steps; top molding and rail edge damaged between the second and third floors.
Living room: parquet scraped, scratched and gouged; decorative border missing inlay pieces and stained; finish worn through in places.
Dining room: paint blotches, gouges and a large stain on the parquet; damaged parquet corners; antique hearth tiles missing and broken; mahogany mantel damaged; a large piece of the doorway casing damaged or missing.
Office: carpet heavily stained; floor scratched. Mahogany window sills throughout: stains, ring marks and gouges.
West master suite: large dark stains on the plank floor, including in front of the fireplace, with a urine odor; scrapes and gouges; soot staining on the wall, ceiling, mantel and shelving; a deep gouge in the molding.
East master bedroom: ceiling damaged where the period chandeliers were replaced with the tenants' fixtures. East bathroom ceiling stained and damaged.
Third floor: southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing pulled away, with protruding nails and torn wood; not safe to use. Northeast storage-ladder railing scraped. Northeast bedroom plank floor with a dark urine stain; bedroom door broken and the plaster behind it damaged. Bathroom tub porcelain chipped and vanity panel broken. Great-room plank floor heavily stained and gouged with a urine odor; plaster damage and staining down one wall; ceiling damaged around the light fixtures.
Karen Liu also noted odors in several rooms.

workPlan.title: Triplex restoration for marketing and move-in readiness
workPlan.summary: Proceed with the restoration work that is already quoted to address the documented move-out damage: refinish and repair floors, repair and refinish the main stair, complete plaster repair and soot cleanup, repaint, restore woodwork and fireplaces, make listed bathroom repairs, then install the new stair runner and replace the office carpet after dusty work is complete.
workPlan.desiredOutcome: Restore the triplex to a clean, safe, move-in ready condition suitable for late October showings and a December 1 move-in, by addressing the documented floor, stair, finish, odor, bathroom, and carpet conditions remaining after move-out.
scope: Sand and refinish the parquet and plank floors throughout the triplex, including final finish suitable for marketing and move-in.
Replace damaged parquet and missing inlay border pieces with matched materials and integrate repairs into the refinished floor.
Treat and seal urine-stained plank floor areas to address staining and lingering odor before applying the finish coats.
Plaster repair and soot cleanup in the rooms noted as damaged and soot-stained, ready for painting.
Paint walls, ceilings and trim throughout, including the ceiling areas damaged around light fixtures, to a uniform move-in ready finish.
Restore damaged woodwork and fireplaces, including window sills, doorway casing, moldings, mantels and the foyer door veneer, to match existing finishes.
Complete the listed bathroom repairs, including tub chip repair, vanity panel repair and recaulk as needed, to a clean functional condition.
Repair and refinish the main stair, including newel post, trim, top molding and rail edge, to remove chips and gouges and restore an even finish.
Supply and install a new stair runner, including removal and disposal of the existing runner.
Replace the office carpet, including removal and disposal of the existing carpet.
workPlan.rationale: The latest condition report shows the loft ladder railing issue is satisfied, but all other major deficiencies remain. The quoted scopes directly match the conditions documented in the move-out walk-through and the restoration assessment report. The owner has set aside $65,000 for restoration and authorized approving work within those funds; the combined quoted scope totals $59,689.33, within the set-aside. Sequencing should keep sanding, plaster repair, and painting ahead of carpet installation to avoid new finishes being damaged or dirtied.

content.title: Restoration assessment and loft railing safety repair
content.summary: Proceed with Feld Architecture’s restoration assessment to produce the condition schedule and scoped repair plan, and complete the urgent loft-ladder railing repair so the area can be used safely for future work and showings.

Prepare a room by room condition and quantity schedule with photos and measurements suitable for scoping the restoration trades.

messages.title: Quote request: Plaster, paint and woodwork
messages.body:
Hello,

Please provide a formal quote for plaster repair and soot cleanup, painting walls and ceilings and trim throughout including ceiling repairs at the light fixtures, restoration of woodwork and fireplaces (including window sills, doorway casing, moldings, mantels, hearth tiles, foyer door veneer, and the northeast bedroom door), and the bathroom repairs listed (tub chip repair and vanity panel and caulking). Please confirm earliest start date, estimated on-site duration, and any dependencies you need completed first, especially regarding floor finishing and stair work. Please also confirm how you will address lingering odors in the rooms noted as having urine odor, if that is part of your scope or exclusions.

Thanks,
Whitcomb Holdings

messages.title: Quote request: Floor restoration
messages.body:
Hello,

Please provide a formal quote to sand and refinish the triplex parquet and plank floors (about 900 square feet), replace damaged parquet and missing inlay border pieces with matched stock, and treat and seal urine-stained plank floors to address staining and odor. Please confirm earliest start date, number of on-site days, what areas must be kept fully clear, and how you prefer other trades to sequence before and after your work.

Thanks,
Whitcomb Holdings

messages.title: Quote request: Restoration assessment
messages.body:
Hello,

Please provide a formal quote for your restoration assessment (site visit up to three hours, room-by-room condition schedule with photos and measurements, written repair scope by trade with preliminary budget, and immediate safety flags). Please confirm earliest site visit availability this week and that the report can be delivered within two business days of the visit. Also confirm any access, measurement, or photo requirements for the assessment.

Thanks,
Whitcomb Holdings

messages.title: Quote request: Loft railing repair
messages.body:
Hello,

Please provide a formal quote to rebuild and secure the southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing that has pulled away and has protruding nails. Please include your scope for removal and rebuild, fastening method, and how you will test it under load. Please confirm your earliest date and the expected on-site duration. Access is by appointment with the owner holding keys; please confirm what you need us to do to keep the area safe until you complete the repair.

Thanks,
Whitcomb Holdings

messages.title: Quote request: Stair repair and refinishing
messages.body:
Hello,

Please provide a formal quote to repair and refinish the main stair, newel post, trim, top molding, and rail edge that are chipped and damaged. Please include how you will protect adjacent floors and walls, expected on-site duration, and earliest start date. If you recommend sequencing this work before or after floor sanding and finishing, please note that in your quote.

Thanks,
Whitcomb Holdings

messages.title: Quote request: Stair runner and office carpet
messages.body:

Please provide a formal quote to supply and install a new stair runner and to replace the office carpet, including removal and disposal of existing materials. Please confirm earliest installation date assuming floor restoration is completed first, and confirm any lead time needed for materials and ordering. Please also confirm how you will protect freshly finished floors during installation.

Thanks,
Whitcomb Holdings
